original_query: select  min(i_item_id)  ,min(i_item_desc)  ,min(s_store_id)  ,min(s_store_name)  ,min(ss_net_profit)  ,min(sr_net_loss)  ,min(cs_net_profit)  ,min(ss_item_sk)  ,min(sr_ticket_number)  ,min(cs_order_number)  from  store_sales  ,store_returns  ,catalog_sales  ,date_dim d1  ,date_dim d2  ,date_dim d3  ,store  ,item  where  d1.d_moy = 9  and d1.d_year = 1999  and d1.d_date_sk = ss_sold_date_sk  and i_item_sk = ss_item_sk  and s_store_sk = ss_store_sk  and ss_customer_sk = sr_customer_sk  and ss_item_sk = sr_item_sk  and ss_ticket_number = sr_ticket_number  and sr_returned_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk  and d2.d_moy               between 9 and  9 + 2  and d2.d_year              = 1999  and sr_customer_sk = cs_bill_customer_sk  and sr_item_sk = cs_item_sk  and cs_sold_date_sk = d3.d_date_sk  and d3.d_moy               between 9 and  9 + 2  and d3.d_year              = 1999  ;
rewritten_query:
select min(i_item_id), min(i_item_desc), min(s_store_id), min(s_store_name), min(ss_net_profit), min(sr_net_loss), min(cs_net_profit), min(ss_item_sk), min(sr_ticket_number), min(cs_order_number)
from store_sales
join date_dim d1 on d1.d_date_sk = ss_sold_date_sk and d1.d_moy = 9 and d1.d_year = 1999
join item i on i.i_item_sk = ss_item_sk
join store s on s.s_store_sk = ss_store_sk
join store_returns sr on sr.sr_customer_sk = ss_customer_sk and sr.sr_item_sk = ss_item_sk and sr.sr_ticket_number = ss_ticket_number
join date_dim d2 on d2.d_date_sk = sr.sr_returned_date_sk and d2.d_moy between 9 and 11 and d2.d_year = 1999
join catalog_sales cs on cs.cs_bill_customer_sk = sr.sr_customer_sk and cs.cs_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
join date_dim d3 on d3.d_date_sk = cs.cs_sold_date_sk and d3.d_moy between 9 and 11 and d3.d_year = 1999;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Folded the constant expression `9 + 2` to `11` in both `d_moy` filters, making range predicates explicit for the optimizer and statistics.
Converted implicit comma joins into explicit JOIN syntax with local (filter) predicates pushed into the JOIN ON clauses, improving readability without changing semantics.

The plan already drives from the selective d2/store_returns date index into store_sales via the (item, ticket) key, then probes catalog_sales by (customer, item); this join order is retained as it is near-optimal.
Rejected CTE/IN-subquery rewrites: the prior rewrite report shows CTE materialization increases estimated cost by ~15.5% (40512 vs 35069), so no subquery restructuring is applied.
